oneLine: Physically careful and clean (siren timing, speed-of-sound delays, no clipping, no clicks), but the barrage has no weight: booms barely move the meter under the siren, with an LRA of 3.6 LU across the trailer salvo. Synth tells remain (sine-sweep kicks, a pure-sine 55 Hz bed that dominates the lulls), and siren level and filtering stay frozen while the camera moves.
strengths: Siren matches the design. The measured contour is 339-708 Hz with a 4.40-4.44 s period (design 330-720 Hz / 4.6 s) and a spin-up. It starts on alert:start plus d/343 (0.22-0.7 s at Arad). Arad north and south-east stagger in through relay offsets, and Nevatim and Dimona arrive +21 s and +42 s later. Insects cut cleanly at the siren (alert spectrogram, about 160-162 s).
The siren is band-limited (custom PeriodicWave, no aliasing visible up to 16 kHz). A second voice detuned by 0.45% gives multi-driver beating, and building slapback taps plus a convolver add space.

Speed-of-sound arrival is solved against the moving listener. Onset alignment has a median error of 3.4 ms in my salvo render (10/15 audible events matched) and 22.9 ms on the moving trailer track. Movers use retarded positions, which gives real Doppler.

Mix hygiene: 0 clipped samples in all three of my renders (peak -3.8 dBFS in the salvo), console clean, and no voice stealing needed (max 8 one-shots). My >11 kHz transient scan found no spurious clicks: every HF transient lines up with a scheduled launch crack. All envelopes start with 'set 0' then a linear attack, and voice kill uses setTargetAtTime (12 ms).

Per-instance variation is seeded per event (random buffer offsets, ±14% duration, filter and level jitter). Per-layer launch recipes differ (Sling has a second pulse, Arrow is long and low). The Shahed loop is physically grounded: 112 rev/s, 4-cylinder two-stroke firing at about 448 Hz, 2x prop blade-pass, jitter and misfires.
Far impact at 6.6 km reads correctly as rumble: spectral centroid 71 Hz, HF -5.7 dB, LF +8.3 dB vs the preceding bed (salvo 254.9 s). Tail length grows with distance.
Honest, rich critic tooling: meta.json records why every unvoiced event was skipped (e.g. 19 Arrow kills marked 'high-altitude, inaudible').

issues.text: The barrage has no weight. With the trailer camera across the salvo (200-240 s), 17 intercepts and impacts leave short-term loudness flat at about -28 LUFS (LRA 3.6 LU). The biggest event, an impact at 1.8 km, adds only +3.7 dB broadband. Intercepts at 5-8 km add 0 to +2 dB. In the street render (205-232 s), no boom raises the broadband level by more than 0.9 dB under the siren. The loudest thing in the mission is the siren, at -16 LUFS short-term. In CoH3 and WARNO, explosions punch 10-20 LU above the bed. Here the climax plays as a steady siren drone.
issues.fix: In src/audio/engine.js blast(), split the boom into (a) a near crack/body using the current ref/d law and (b) an LF rumble layer (<250 Hz) with its own, larger ref (e.g. 1500*size) or a d^-0.7 law, so distant intercepts keep low-end weight. Raise blast power about 8-10 dB relative to siren power: either drop POLES power from 0.26 to about 0.12 in offline.js, or add power≈2.5 to blast voices. Add a sidechain duck: on each blast arrival, automate bus.siren and bus.amb gain down by 3-6 dB (scaled by distGain*size, 30 ms attack, 0.8-1.2 s release), in both offline.js and index.js. Target: intercepts at 5 km read +6-10 dB momentary over the siren bed.

issues.text: Siren level and air filtering are frozen at the listener distance at alert start. E.siren() sets g.gain = distGain(d) and air = airCut(d) once, and the panner has rolloffFactor 0. Panning a 75 s siren from Arad out to Nevatim (7 km), or flying the trailer camera, never changes its loudness or brightness. In the trailer render, the Arad poles stay at a constant -23.5 dB with the d=2.4 km start distance. This fails TARGET §3: 'sources pan and attenuate correctly as the camera moves.' Long launch voices (Arrow 8.5 s) are frozen at the pad position in the same way.
issues.fix: Return { g, air, pos, ref, power } from E.siren() and automate them like movers. In offline.js, add a 10 Hz loop over meta.sirens that sets g.gain = distGain(dist(L.at(toSim(c)).p, pos), ref)*power and air.frequency = airCut(d) (retarded time is fine to ignore for a static source). In index.js update(), use setTargetAtTime at 4 Hz. Have launch voices follow a rising position, e.g. panner position automated along +y at about 300-600 m/s over dur.

issues.text: Blast and launch bodies are sine sweeps: crack() adds a sine at 150→42 Hz, and blast() adds a sine at 58→22 Hz. This is the classic 808-kick tell, and every launch and every boom carries the same tonal 'doom' shape. The code comment promises an N-wave, but crack() is a high-passed white-noise spit, not an N-wave.
issues.fix: Replace the sine body with brown or pink noise through a lowpass whose cutoff sweeps from about 400 to 40 Hz, plus a 2-3 partial inharmonic cluster (e.g. 31/47/73 Hz with random ±15% detune per instance), or drop the oscillator entirely and lift the brown-noise body. Implement a real N-wave in dsp.js: a 1.5-4 ms linear +A→-A ramp buffer with very short rise times, its length scaled by size, played through the air filter. Reserve the sine thump for UI only.

issues.text: The tension bed is pure sines: 55, 55.35 and 82.41 Hz, plus static triangle chords at the all-clear. In the post-siren lull (238-246 s), the 55 Hz line alone is -37 dB against a total of -32.6 dB, so a single pure sine carries about 36% of the energy. The 82.8 Hz line adds another -40 dB. It is visible as a constant bright band across every spectrogram. On headphones or a sub, this reads as an electrical hum, not a score.
issues.evidence: status/audio/audio-r1c/salvo/spectrogram.png (bright 55/82 Hz bands); tone analysis of salvo audio 238.5-246.5 s
issues.fix: In engine.js ambience(), build the bed from 2-3 detuned saws or filtered pink noise through a lowpass at about 200-400 Hz, with slow cutoff LFOs (0.03-0.08 Hz). Alternatively, use a bowed-noise texture: pink → bandpass at 55/82 Hz with Q≈20. Lower the impactWindow bed target from 0.13 to about 0.06, and leave the low end to the booms. Give the all-clear chord a slow attack and filter movement.

issues.text: High-frequency loss with distance is too gentle. airCut() feeds a single 12 dB/oct biquad, and the crack's 'near' term reaches out to 4.4 km. An impact at 2.7 km therefore still prints a crack up to 16 kHz (white line at 209.8 s in the salvo spectrogram), and Sling launches at 1 km show crackle up to 16 kHz. Real air absorption removes nearly everything above about 4 kHz by 2-3 km.
issues.fix: In engine.js voice(), cascade two lowpass biquads (24 dB/oct) at airCut(d), or add a highshelf of -0.004*d dB above 4 kHz. Change crack near = clamp(1 - (d - 300)/1500, 0, 1). Give the movers' lp in E.mover() the same second stage.

issues.text: Incoming ballistic missiles make no sound until impact. The recorder skips th.type === 'ballistic' (index.js:145), and nothing synthesizes the re-entry. The tearing roar and sonic-boom double crack of descending re-entry vehicles is the defining sound of the Nevatim strikes. Jets are generic filtered noise, without the ground-reflection comb 'flange' that makes a flyby read as a jet.
issues.fix: Add an E.reentry(e, t, d, r) one-shot scheduled about 3-6 s before each ballistic impact (or from the threat's terminal track). It should contain an N-wave double boom (a supersonic shock arrives before the roar), then 2-4 s of tearing noise (pink → bandpass 300-900 Hz, AM at 20-40 Hz), falling into the impact. For jets in E.mover(), mix the source with a copy delayed by τ = 2h_listener·sinθ/C (automated in offline.js from geometry) to get the moving comb filter.

issues.text: The siren contour is a sharp-cornered triangle in log-frequency, because exp ramps produce V-shaped turns at 340 and 708 Hz. The amplitude is perfectly constant, so the short-term level holds flat at about -18.5 LUFS for 25 s in the alert render. Real sirens round off at the turnarounds (motor or driver inertia), and distant poles flutter with wind and turbulence. The constant level also makes the alert beat static for its full ~75 s.
issues.fix: In E.siren(), drive the frequency with setValueCurveAtTime using a raised-cosine or first-order-lag curve per half-cycle (about 15% rounding at the extremes). Add a slow random AM (0.1-0.5 Hz, ±2-4 dB), stronger for the Nevatim and Dimona poles (scaled by d/3000), plus a small lowpass wobble on distant poles.

issues.text: The live siren stop() uses cancelScheduledValues and then setTargetAtTime. If phase 'hold' arrives during the 3.6 s wind-down (likely at 2-4x sim speed, since the siren is scheduled in real time), the exponential ramp is cancelled and the gain jumps back to 1, which pops. Pitch also stays mid-sweep instead of spinning down. At 4x, the siren also outlives its countdown, because cycles are computed in sim seconds but played in real seconds.
issues.fix: Use env.gain.cancelAndHoldAtTime(at) (with a fallback to setValueAtTime(env.gain.value, at)) before the release. Also cancelAndHold both oscillators' frequency and ramp exponentially to 0.4*fLo over 3 s. Scale nCycles by 1/clock.speed at trigger time, or stop the sirens on alert:impactWindow.

issues.text: Rendered windows start and end mid-waveform: the salvo WAV's first sample is about -19 dBFS (-3573/-2941). A capture muxed from audioOffline() will start with a click.
issues.fix: In offline.js, after trimming the pre-roll, apply a 5 ms raised-cosine fade-in and fade-out to ch[0] and ch[1] before encodeWav (an option that defaults to on for captures).

issues.text: Every source shares one convolver IR, with fixed discrete slaps at 0.31, 0.57, 1.04 and 1.6 s. Every boom and launch therefore gets the same echo rhythm, independent of where it happened. The cricket loops (7.31 s and 11.07 s) and the 19.7 s wind loop repeat exactly. The wind seam uses a linear crossfade of uncorrelated noise, which dips about 3 dB.
issues.fix: Generate 2-3 IR variants and pick one per voice by azimuth or distance, or replace the fixed slap taps with per-blast delay taps computed from distance to the escarpment and town edge, inside blast(). Use an equal-power crossfade at the wind seam, and add a third cricket loop (prime length) or per-loop random gain LFOs.

benchmarkNotes: WARNO: its strength is distance-layered artillery, with a crack near and a long rolling rumble far, which always cuts through the bed. Iron Wall has the right architecture (near/far layering, speed-of-sound delay, distance-scaled tails, a far impact centroid of 71 Hz) but loses the cut-through test: booms are 0-4 dB events under a continuous siren, where WARNO's would be 10-20 LU spikes. CoH3: it relies on varied, organic one-shots and tasteful ducking. Iron Wall has good per-instance seeding and siren ducking of ambience, but sine-sweep kick bodies and a pure-sine bed betray synthesis in a way CoH3's recorded and processed material never does. The siren itself (band-limited, multi-pole phasing, slapback, staggered distant towns) is the strongest element and is plausibly better than either reference has for this kind of cue. Spatial correctness is half there: delays and Doppler are right, but levels stay frozen for long sources as the camera moves.

verified: Rendered alert (150-190), salvo (205-262) and trailer track (200-240, moving listener) myself to status/audio/audio-r1c/; read all three spectrograms, report.json and meta.json; no console errors.
0 clipped samples; peaks -7.5 / -3.8 / -10.6 dBFS; integrated -19.8 / -17.5 / -28.4 LUFS; LRA 6.4 / 15.6 / 3.6 LU.
Siren contour 339-708 Hz, period 4.40-4.44 s, measured from the WAV; it starts at alert:start + d/343.
Onset alignment: median 3.4 ms (salvo, fixed) and 22.9 ms (track); 10 of 15 audible events matched (salvo).
No spurious HF clicks: every >11 kHz transient matched a scheduled launch crack, except sample 0 of the salvo window.
Per-event loudness and spectral deltas (my numpy analysis): booms at 2.7-8 km add ≤ +3.7 dB broadband; the far impact at 6.6 km has a 71 Hz centroid.
Tonal analysis: 55 Hz and 82.8 Hz bed sines dominate the post-siren lull; Shahed harmonic lines are visible at about 1.47 kHz and 366 Hz before the alert.
notVerifiable: Whether the siren timbre actually sounds like an Israeli civil-defence siren rather than a synth: the spectrum and contour are right, but perceived 'horn' character can't be judged from a spectrogram.
Whether the Shahed loop reads as a moped or lawnmower, or as a buzzy synth; whether launches sound like a rocket 'rip' or like filtered noise.
Perceived punch and weight of booms on real speakers or headphones (measured deltas are small, but transient perception differs from 400 ms loudness).
Live (AudioContext) path behaviour: I reviewed it in code only, including equal-power panning without HRTF, the per-frame CPU of update() (≤0.3 ms budget), and node leaks during long play.
Panning correctness while rotating the camera (stereo correlation 0.65-0.87 suggests a moderate stereo image, but not whether directions are right).
Whether repetition of the 2 s Shahed loop or the cricket loops is audible over minutes.
